A polygraph machine, also known as a “lie detector,” is a common part of criminal investigations. The instrument is used to measure [[21]] a person’s body reacts to questions. The theory underlying it is that lying is stressful, and that this stress can be measured and recorded on a polygraph machine.
When a person takes a polygraph test, four to six wires, called sensors, are [[22]] to different parts of his body. The sensors pick up signals from the person’s blood pressure, pulse, and perspiration. [[23]] the process of questioning, all the signals are recorded on a single strip of moving paper. Once the questions are finished, the examiner analyzes the results to determine if the person tested [[24]] truthful.
Well-trained examiners can usually detect lying with a high degree of [[25]] when they use a polygraph. However, because different people behave differently when lying, a polygraph test is by no means perfect.

groups.passage:
In Japan, a person’s blood type is popularly believed to decide his/her temperament and personality. Type-A people are generally considered sensitive perfectionists and good team players, but over-anxious. Type Os are curious and generous but stubborn. Type ABs are artistic but mysterious and unpredictable, and type Bs are cheerful but eccentric, individualistic, and selfish. Though lacking scientific evidence, this belief is widely seen in books, magazines, and television shows.
The blood-type belief has been used in unusual ways. The women’s softball team that won gold for Japan at the Beijing Olympics is reported to have used blood-type theories to customize training for each player. Some kindergartens have adopted teaching methods along blood group lines, and even major companies reportedly make decisions about assignments based on an employee’s blood type. In 1990, Mitsubishi Electronics was reported to have announced the formation of a team composed entirely of AB workers, thanks to “their ability to make plans.”
The belief even affects politics. One former prime minister considered it important enough to reveal in his official profile that he was a type A, while his opposition rival was type B. In 2011, a minister, Ryu Matsumoto, was forced to resign after only a week in office, when a bad-tempered encounter with local officials was televised. In his resignation speech, he blamed his failings on the fact that he was blood type B.
The blood-type craze, considered simply harmless fun by some Japanese, may manifest itself as prejudice and discrimination. In fact, this seems so common that the Japanese now have a term for it: bura-hara, meaning blood-type harassment. There are reports of discrimination leading to children being bullied, ending of happy relationships, and loss of job opportunities due to blood type.

options.A: He revealed his rival’s blood type.
options.B: He was seen behaving rudely on TV.
options.C: He blamed his failings on local officials.
options.D: He was discriminated against because of blood type.

questions.stem: Which field is NOT mentioned in the passage as being affected by blood-type beliefs?

groups.passage:
Like many other five-year-olds, Jeanie Low of Houston, Texas, would use a stool to help her reach the bathroom sink. However, the plastic step-stool she had at home was unstable and cluttered up the small bathroom shared by her whole family. After learning of an invention contest held by her school that year, Jeanie resolved to enter the contest by creating a stool that would be a permanent fixture in the bathroom, and yet could be kept out of the way when not in use.
Jeanie decided to make a stool attached to the bathroom cabinet door under the sink. She cut a plank of wood into two pieces, each about two feet wide and one foot long. Using metal hinges, Jeanie attached one piece of the wood to the front of the cabinet door, and the second piece to the first. The first piece was set just high enough so that when it swung out horizontally from the cabinet door, the second piece would swing down from the first, just touching the ground, and so serving as a support for the first piece of the wood. This created a convenient, sturdy platform for any person too short to reach the sink. When not in use, the hinges allowed the two pieces of wood to fold back up tightly against the cabinet, where they were held in place by magnets. Jeanie called her invention the “Kiddie Stool.”
Jeanie’s Kiddie Stool won first place in her school’s contest. Two years later, it was awarded first prize again at Houston’s first annual Invention Fair. As a result, Jeanie was invited to make a number of public appearances with her Kiddie Stool, and was featured on local TV as well as in newspapers. Many people found the story of the Kiddie Stool inspiring because it showed that with imagination, anyone can be an inventor.

groups.passage:
Ongoing conflicts across the Middle East have prevented more than 13 million children from attending school, according to a report published by UNICEF, the United Nations Children’s Fund.
The report states that 40% of all children across the region are currently not receiving an education, which is a result of two consequences of violence: structural damage to schools and the displacement of populations, also called “forced migration.” Both issues result from the tide of violence that has crossed the region in recent years. The report examines nine countries where a state of war has become the norm. Across these countries, violence has made 8,500 schools unusable. In certain cases, communities have relied on school buildings to function as shelters for the displaced, with up to nine families living in a single classroom in former schools across Iraq.
The report pays particularly close attention to Syria, where a bloody civil war has displaced at least nine million people since the war began in 2011. With the crisis now in its fifth year, basic public services, including education, inside Syria have been stretched to breaking point. Within the country, the quality and availability of education depends on whether a particular region is suffering violence.
The report concludes with an earnest request to international policymakers to distribute financial and other resources to ease the regional crisis. With more than 13 million children already driven from classrooms by conflict, it is no exaggeration to say that the educational prospects of a generation of children are in the balance. The forces that are crushing individual lives and futures are also destroying the prospects for an entire region.

groups.passage:
Many marine animals, including penguins and marine iguanas, have evolved ways to get rid of excess salt by using special salt-expelling glands around their tongue. However, the sea snake’s salt glands cannot handle the massive amounts of salt that would enter their bodies if they actually drank seawater. This poses a serious problem when it comes to getting enough water to drink. If seawater is not an option, how does this animal survive in the ocean?
An international team of researchers focused on a population of yellow-bellied sea snakes living near Costa Rica, where rain often does not fall for up to seven months out of the year. Because yellow-bellied sea snakes usually spend all of their time far from land, rain is the animals’ only source of fresh water. When it rains, a thin layer of fresh water forms on top of the ocean, providing the snakes with a fleeting opportunity to lap up that precious resource. But during the dry season when there is no rain, snakes presumably have nothing to drink. Thus, the team became interested in testing whether sea snakes became dehydrated at sea.
The researchers collected more than 500 yellow-bellied sea snakes and weighed them. They found that during the dry season about half of the snakes accepted fresh water offered to them, while nearly none did during the wet season. A snake’s likelihood to drink also correlated with its body condition, with more withered snakes being more likely to drink, and to drink more. Finally, as predicted, snakes captured during the dry season contained significantly less body water than those scooped up in the rainy season. Thus, it seems the snake is able to endure certain degrees of dehydration in between rains. Scientists believe that dehydration at sea may explain the declining populations of sea snakes in some parts of the world.

options.A: To test if sea snakes lose body water at sea.
options.B: To see whether sea snakes drink water offered to them.
options.C: To find out if sea snakes are greatly reduced in population.
options.D: To prove that sea snakes drink only water coming from rivers.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about sea snakes?

options.D: They usually live near the coastal area where there is more fresh water.

questions.stem: Which of the following is one of the findings of the study?

options.B: If captured in the wet season, sea snakes drank a lot of fresh water.
options.C: Most of the sea snakes had lost a lot of body water when captured.
options.D: Dehydration is not a problem among sea snakes since they live at sea.

questions.stem: What can be inferred from the study?

options.A: Sea snakes can easily survive long years of drought.
options.B: Evolution will very likely enable sea snakes to drink seawater.
options.C: Sea snakes will be the last creature affected by global warming.
options.D: The sea snakes’ population distribution is closely related to rainfall.

questions.scoring_notes:
評分標準與歷年相同，在「中譯英」部分，每小題總分 4 分，原則上是每個錯誤扣 0.5 分。
今年的「中譯英」題目反映當代現象與考生的生活貼近，點出相較於父母的世代，現在的年輕人享受較多自由及繁榮，但在快速變化的世界中，也必須學習有效地因應新的挑戰。評量的重點在於考生能否運用常用的詞彙與基本句型將兩句中文翻譯成正確達意的英文句子，所測驗之句型為高中生熟悉的範圍，詞彙亦控制在大考中心詞彙表四級內之詞彙，中等程度以上的考生，如果能使用正確句型並注意用字、拼字，應能得理想的分數。例如：「相較於他們父母的世代」若譯成 in comparison with their parents’ generation 即可得分；「學習如何有效地因應新的挑戰」則可翻譯為 learn (how) to react to new challenges effectively，這兩句的介係詞片語均可放在主要子句前面或後面。評閱抽樣卷時，我們發現有不少考生對於英文詞彙的語意及使用，以及英文拼字仍有加強的空間，如第一句的「繁榮」有許多考生未譯，或者拼字錯誤；「父母的世代」忘了所有格的使用；「必須」可用 must / should 後面就不可加 to；「有效地」是 effectively，有不少考生翻譯為 efficiently，對詞彙語意的掌握還需加強；「挑戰」challenges 拼字錯誤的考生也不少，相當可惜。

patterns: Compared with/to ... / In comparison with ...（相較於）

sections.instructions:
說明︰1.依提示在「答案卷」上寫一篇英文作文。
2.文長至少120個單詞（words）。

questions.label: 作文
questions.stem: 提示︰你認為家裡生活環境的維持應該是誰的責任?請寫一篇短文說明你的看法。文分兩段，第一段說明你對家事該如何分工的看法及理由，第二段舉例說明你家中家事分工的情形，並描述你自己做家事的經驗及感想。
questions.scoring_notes:
「英文作文」的評分標準是依據內容、組織、文法句構、詞彙拼字、體例五個項目給分，字數明顯不足的作文則扣總分 1 分。
第二大題是「英文作文」，以至少 120 個單詞寫 2 段，第一段寫對家事分工的看法及理由，第二段說明自己家中家事分工及做家事的經驗及感想。
今年的「英文作文」為主題式引導寫作，有 2 個寫作任務，跳脫「看圖寫作」的模式，雖與過去幾年的看四格漫畫敘述故事之命題方式不同，但家事分工與考生生活貼近，要考生第一段寫對家事分工的看法及理由，第二段說明自己家中家事分工及做家事的經驗及感想，有點提醒年輕人在家裡要分擔家事的期許。寫作內容必須完成提示中要求的 2 項寫作任務才算內容完整，有些考生只寫出對家事分工的看法及理由，未寫自己做家事的經驗及感想；有些考生只描述自己做家事的經驗及感想，未說明對家事分工的看法及理由，這樣就是未完成提示中要求的寫作任務，內容及組織均會扣分。大致只要寫作任務能完整完成，條理說明看法與理由，同時敘述自己的經驗及感想，就能拿到不錯的分數。評分的考量重點為作文內容是否切題並有足夠的細節、組織是否具連貫性、句子結構及用字是否適切、以及拼字與標點符號的使用是否正確得當。

tags.topic: who should be responsible for housework: views on dividing household chores, and one’s own family’s division of chores and experience doing them

extraction.method: 題本文字以 Word 版 paper-2.docx 為主（以程式走訪 document.xml 所有 w:r，含巢狀於其他元素內的 run；有底線的數字 run 合併後轉成 [[題號]]），再以程式將全部 276 個文字欄位（大題標題、部分標題、說明、題組標示、選文各段、題幹、選項、選項庫）去空白後與 pdftotext -layout（paper-1.pdf）比對，全部為 PDF 原文子字串；反向檢查 PDF 扣除上述欄位後只剩封面、頁首頁尾與題號，確認無遺漏；Read 看 PDF 全部 8 頁頁面影像確認版面、粗體／斜體與底線，並確認本卷沒有任何圖表；答案取自 answer.pdf（pdftotext -layout，並看頁面影像核對）；評分原則取自 scoring.pdf（pdftotext 逐行接合，並以兩頁頁面影像核對）逐字摘錄；統計以 xlrd 讀 stats-1.xls（英文工作表：答對率 P、高分組 Ph、低分組 Pl、鑑別度 D）、stats-2.xls（英文工作表：選項分析 T／H／L 列、未答）、stats-3.xls（英文科非選擇題分數人數統計表），並以程式交叉核對（選項分析標 * 的選項＝官方答案；其 T／H／L 比例與 P／Ph／Pl 相符或差 1 個百分點；D＝Ph−Pl；非選擇題各分數段人數加總＝到考人數）。
issues: 結構核對：與 gsat-spec.json legacy_gsat 期別「94–110」一致——詞彙題 1–15（15分）、綜合測驗 16–30（3篇×5題，題組標示16–20、21–25、26–30，15分）、文意選填 31–40（A–J，10分）、閱讀測驗 41–56（4篇×4題，每題2分，32分）、中譯英 2題×4分、英文作文 20分（文長至少120個單詞）；第壹部分單選題 72分＋第貳部分非選擇題 28分＝100分；封面「考試時間：100 分鐘」「單選題共 56 題」「非選擇題共二大題」。無差異。
validator warning「題號重複 [1, 2]」為預期：中譯英兩題題本編為 1.、2.，英文作文沒有題號（no 填 1）；no 必須是整數，故沿用題本編號，並以 label「中譯英1」「中譯英2」「作文」區分，label 無重複（與 gsat-106 等檔做法相同）。

中譯英：評分原則沒有公布完整參考譯文，只給了兩個片語的可得分譯法（「相較於他們父母的世代」→ in comparison with their parents’ generation；「學習如何有效地因應新的挑戰」→ learn (how) to react to new challenges effectively）並指出常見錯誤（「繁榮」漏譯或拼錯、「父母的世代」漏所有格、must / should 後加 to、「有效地」誤用 efficiently、challenges 拼錯），故 answer 與 accepted_answers 皆為 null，片語譯法保留在 scoring_notes。評分原則中與中譯英相關的段落同時談到兩句，無法逐句切開而不破壞原文，故兩題的 scoring_notes 都放「評分標準與歷年相同…每個錯誤扣 0.5 分。」加上整段中譯英說明（逐字）。

英文作文：評分原則沒有官方範文，answer 為 null。題目「文分兩段」，tags.paragraphs=2；essay_type 依 gsat-107、gsat-108 同類「主題寫作、文分兩段」題的做法標 topic（評分原則稱「主題式引導寫作，有 2 個寫作任務」）。scoring_notes 由評分原則三處逐字摘錄組成（「英文作文」評分標準句、第一段中「第二大題是「英文作文」，以至少 120 個單詞寫 2 段…」、最後一段作文說明），以換行分隔。本年作文評分項目仍為五項（內容、組織、文法句構、詞彙拼字、體例），與 spec 所記 106 年起改為四項的變動一致。

非選擇題統計：stats-3.xls 只有「第一題（中譯英，滿分8分，兩小題合計）」與「第二題（英文作文，滿分20分）」的分數人數分布，無法拆到中譯英各小題，因此放在 sections[s5].stats 與 sections[s6].stats 的 score_distribution（schema 未定義此欄位，沿用 gsat-106/107/109 的做法）；rate 為原表百分比÷100，分母是報名人數 135,583（含缺考 2,399；到考 133,184），已核對兩題各分數段人數加總＝到考人數 133,184。原表分數區間「9.00- 9.99」等的空白已去除；作文最高分段「20.00-20.99」僅 1 人，原表百分比 0.00，rate 照原表填 0.0。小題層級 stats 為 null。

選擇題統計：除 schema 欄位外，另存 option_rates_high／option_rates_low（stats-2.xls 選項分析的高分組 H、低分組 L 列）與 omit_rate（全體未答比例，T 列；第45、56題 T 列未答 1%）；stats-1.xls 的五組通過率 Pa–Pe 與 D1–D4 未收錄。已程式核對全部 56 題：選項分析中標 * 的選項＝官方答案、D＝Ph−Pl、題號對齊無誤。兩表有 3 處相差 1 個百分點（四捨五入差異）：第16題低分組 stats-1 Pl=57、stats-2 L 列正答 58；第39題低分組 Pl=12、L 列 13；第55題高分組 Ph=66、H 列 67。correct_rate／high_group／low_group／discrimination 一律取 stats-1，option_rates*／omit_rate 一律取 stats-2，未互相改動。各題 T／H／L 列選項比例加未答因四捨五入加總為 0.98–1.02。

低答對率／低鑑別度題目已複核非對齊錯誤（皆為大考中心原始數據）：第24題 P=0.26、D=0.20（45% 選 B would be，高分組 40% 選 B）；第30題 P=0.30（37% 選 B pulling）；第41題 P=0.46、D=0.15（官方答案 C Objective，30% 選 A Negative，高分組 39% 選 A）；第43題 P=0.32（31% 選 D）；第53題 P=0.31（41% 選 B）；第51題 P=0.37、D=0.27；第55題 P=0.37；第26題 D=0.31（35% 選 A them）。
第43題題幹寫「Prime Minister Ryu Matsumoto」，但選文寫的是「a minister, Ryu Matsumoto」（選文另提到的 prime minister 是「One former prime minister」，另一人）；題本原文如此，照錄未改，官方答案 B。
格式：題本中第41–44題選文的 bura-hara 為斜體；第42題的 LEAST、第44題的 NOT、第49–52題選文與第50題的 Iraq、選文與第51題的 in the balance 為粗體；「第16至20題為題組」等題組標示有底線。依 schema 不保留粗斜體（第50、51題以引號指稱粗體字，非「畫底線的字」，故未加 <u>）。

文字來源與正規化：Word 版第8題「are so」與第21–25題選文第一段段末含不換行空白（U+00A0），已改為一般空白／去除；Word 版選文內有僅供排版的強制換行（w:br，位於 [[29]]、[[33]]、[[37]]、[[39]] 前），頁面影像確認為同一段落，已改為空白。Word 版第5、11、14題題號、第26–30題選項列題號、第41–56題題號、第43題 (A)–(D) 為自動編號，不在文字中，依 PDF 補齊對應。pdftotext 把第39題所在句的 piece 拆成「piec e」（字距排版造成），Word 版與頁面影像皆為 piece。PDF 選項庫 I、J 印作「( I ) dry」「( J ) true」（括號內有空白），代號統一為 I、J。英文作文提示「應該是誰的責任?請寫」的問號為半形（Word 與 PDF 皆同），照錄。
評分原則逐行接合時，只有一處行尾中文接行首英文：「有不少考生翻譯為」＋「efficiently」，依全文中英文之間留一空白的排版慣例接為「翻譯為 efficiently」；其餘數字與中文之間的空白（如「每小題總分 4 分」）照 pdftotext 輸出保留。評分原則與題本文字皆無 CJK 相容表意字（NFC 正規化前後相同）。

標註判斷：第19題 what 在「what a troublemaker his son was」中作限定詞（感嘆句型名詞子句），不是代名詞，故只標 grammar／noun_clause、不填 answer_pos；第29題「Without international trade, nations would be limited…」標 grammar／subjunctive（含意假設語氣）；第26題虛受詞 it 依 gsat-85、gsat-87 的做法標 grammar_point=pronoun；第48題（哪句諺語最能表達故事精神）標 main_idea。題組 sdgs 只標明顯相關者（國際貿易→8、17；造林→15；血型歧視→10；中東兒童失學→4、16；海蛇與海洋→14），其餘為空陣列。

本檔新增的非 schema 欄位：section.part_title／part_instructions（第壹、貳部分標題與第貳部分共同說明，放在該部分的第一個大題 s1、s5）、section.stats（非選擇題分數分布）、group.group_label（「第16至20題為題組」等題本原文）、sources.paper_word、question.stats.option_rates_high／option_rates_low／omit_rate。
